In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, and evaluation of a series of mono-, di-, and trisubstituted tetrahydropyran derivatives as potential inhibitors of COX-2 and tumor cell lines.
the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of a novel class of THPs carrying one, two or three aryl ring(s) and other substituants.
the synthesis and evaluation of tetrahydropyran (THP) derivatives as COX-2 inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mono-, di-, and trisubstituted THPs are potent and selective COX-2 inhibitors and also exhibit good antiproliferative activity.
the increase in the molecular weight of THPs from 0 to 2 and 2 to 3 aryl rings increased the COX-2 inhibitory activity, COX-2 selectivity, and antiproliferative activities.
the size and shape of the molecules play an important role in the COX inhibitory activities and selectivity for CO2 over COX1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the compounds with one arlyl group on THP were moderate inhibitors of COX-2, while the compounds with two and three aryl rings were more potent inhibitors of COX2 and also exhibited high selectivity.

the presence of one aryl ring in the THPs resulted in moderate inhibition of COX-2 and COX-1, whereas the presence of two or three aryl groups enhanced their COX-2 inhibitory activity and selectivity.
the presence of one, two, and three aryl rings in THPs enhances their COX-2 inhibitory activities and selectivity over COX-2 in a stepwise fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of two or three aryl moieties on THP is a prerequisite for the design of COX-2 selective inhibitors with good therapeutic indices.
the increase in size of the THP molecule, with the presence of two or three aryl moieties, is responsible for the enhanced COX-2 inhibitory activity as well as COX-2 selectivity over COX- 1.
the presence of two or three aryl groups in the tetrahydropyran ring enhances the COX-2 inhibitory activity and the selectivity of the compound over COX-2.
